subject: The cockroach is asked where he was born, and nobody knows where the movement lives now
alt: Sandeep Adhwaryu’s cartoon: on a white background, at the left, a huge brown cockroach stands upright on two legs like a human. His long antennae are held high and in one leg he holds a black, passport-like document with a golden emblem. The bubble above him says: THEY'RE ASKING WHERE I WAS BORN. At the right stand two young people. The one in front has curly hair, a white T-shirt and blue jeans, a book tucked at his side, and he speaks to the cockroach with an open palm. Behind him a girl with glasses and a ponytail, in a pink kurta and a yellow dupatta, stands holding a book-like object to her chest. The young man’s bubble says: I REMEMBER WHERE THE MOVEMENT WAS BORN. BTW, WHERE DOES IT LIVE THESE DAYS ? Dust and pebbles are scattered on the ground.
chutki: The cockroach, upright on two legs with a passport in hand, complains: they are asking where I was born. One of the two young people standing in front of him with books replies that he remembers where the movement was born; just tell us where it lives these days.

The cartoon puts two questions side by side. One comes from those who ask: where were you born? The cockroach has to explain himself even with a passport in his hand. The other comes from his own friends: the movement whose birthplace everyone remembers, at what address can it be found today? The cockroach is the symbol that became the mark of the young people’s movement, and Sandeep Adhwaryu hands him a passport and puts him in the queue for questioning.
